documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit. Breathing roughly where it was in the fall - stairs slow her down, flat walking OK. Cough only now and then. Joints so-so; rheum keeping the same regimen. No palpitations. Hot flashes controlled. Taking alendronate correctly, no heartburn.

ROS: no fever, weight loss, chest pain, edema, bleeding, bowel change.

Exam: Well. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs: dry crackles both bases, as before. Abdomen benign. Breasts not examined today (mammogram current). Hands with mild MCP swelling. No edema. Neuro: grip mildly reduced bilaterally, otherwise nonfocal; gait normal.

A/P
- RA-ILD: pulmonology yearly, next due in the fall.
- RA: MTX/HCQ/pred, quarterly labs here.
- PAF on amiodarone: TSH/LFTs today.
- Osteoporosis: alendronate year 2, Ca/D.
- Hx breast ca: mammogram 11/2023.
- Atlantoaxial subluxation: no new symptoms; spine surgeon follow-up when due.
- HM: Pap 2022 normal (next 2027). Colonoscopy 2022 normal (next 2032). Vaccines up to date for the season.
RTC 6 months, labs q3mo.

orders.reason: Right hip pain, on chronic prednisone

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled from May; living with and caring for her father.

CC: R hip pain x ~3 wks. Deep ache in the groin and front of the hip, worse when she is on her feet a lot (lots of standing and stairs at her dad's), aches at night too. No fall or injury. No fever.

Exam: walks with a mild limp. R hip: groin pain with internal rotation, rotation limited compared with L. No tenderness over the trochanter. Knee and back exam unremarkable. Distal pulses and sensation normal.

A/P: R hip pain, mechanical, in a woman on long-term prednisone - want ortho to see her soon rather than waiting on films here. Referral placed, marked soon. Ibuprofen as she already uses, plus acetaminophen. Limit stairs where she can. Quarterly MTX labs drawn today.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (1000 mg) by mouth every 8 hours as needed for hip pain

conditions.label: Idiopathic aseptic necrosis of right femur
conditions.note: Right femoral head, with collapse on X-ray

reports.text: AP pelvis and frog-leg lateral right hip. Flattening and loss of height of the right femoral head with subchondral sclerosis. Joint space preserved. Acetabulum normal. Left hip normal. No fracture.
reports.conclusion: Collapse of the right femoral head, consistent with avascular necrosis.

documents.title: Orthopedic surgery consultation
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Visit 8/16/2023, referred by her PCP.

Ms. Parsons, whom we treated for a left distal radius fracture in 2021, has had six weeks of right hip pain that has been steadily worsening. She describes a deep ache, worse with standing and walking, and now present at rest as well. No injury, fever or recent infection.

Exam: internal rotation of the right hip reproduces her pain and range of motion is limited. No swelling, redness or warmth around the hip.

Inflammatory markers and white count drawn today are normal. Radiographs show a flattened, collapsed right femoral head with the joint space still preserved.

Impression: avascular necrosis of the right femoral head, likely related to long-term glucocorticoids.

Plan: we discussed that the head has already collapsed. For now we recommend activity modification, avoiding high-impact activity, and continuing her current analgesics. We will repeat X-rays in six months. Total hip arthroplasty was discussed as a later option if pain or function worsens; she would like to wait.

documents.title: Ophthalmology report
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body: Hydroxychloroquine screening 9/27/2023 (2022 exam 9/2022 also normal). Fields full, SD-OCT without parafoveal change. No toxicity. Return in 12 months.

documents.author: cardiology
documents.body: Seen 11/28/2023. No palpitations or presyncope. ECG sinus rhythm. She is busy caring for her father. Continue amiodarone 200 mg daily with thyroid and liver monitoring through your office. Anticoagulation still not indicated (CHA2DS2-VASc 1). Return in a year.

reports.conclusion: Stable avascular necrosis of the right femoral head.

documents.title: Orthopedic follow-up
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body: Seen 2/21/2024 for right femoral head avascular necrosis. Pain about the same as in August; manageable with her current analgesics and pacing. X-rays unchanged. She is not ready to consider hip replacement. Continue conservative care and return in 6 to 12 months or sooner if worse.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Still the main caregiver for her dad, tiring but she says she would not have it otherwise. Mood OK, PHQ-2 1. Hip pain stable, ortho saw her last week, conservative. Breathing about the same. No palpitations. HT continues per gyn.

Exam: Well, a bit tired-appearing. Heart regular. Lungs: bibasilar dry crackles, unchanged. Mild antalgic gait favoring R. MCP thickening. No edema.

A/P
- RA / RA-ILD: rheum and pulm co-managing; pulm visit due, she will book it.
- AVN R hip: conservative per ortho.
- PAF on amiodarone: TSH/LFTs today.
- Osteoporosis: alendronate year 3.
- Caregiver strain: discussed respite options, she will look into a home aide for a few hours a week.
- HM up to date. Lipids today.
RTC 4-6 months.

documents.body: Normal. Faxed to rheumatology.

documents.title: Getting winded
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is probably nothing. I've been more out of breath since early spring and figured I was just out of shape from being stuck at Dad's. But now I have to stop halfway through watering the greenhouse, which never used to happen. Dry cough too, same as before. No fever. Should I wait for my lung doctor or come in?

documents.title: RE: Getting winded
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Not nothing - please come in so I can listen and check your oxygen. Front desk will call with a time in the next couple of weeks. If you get breathless at rest, chest pain, or fever before then, go to the emergency department.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Breathing worse over ~3 months, initially blamed on deconditioning. Now stops halfway through watering. Persistent dry cough. No fever, chest pain, orthopnea, leg swelling. Last pulm visit 9/2022 - overdue, partly because of caring for her father.

Exam: SpO2 93% RA at rest. Speaking full sentences. Heart regular. Lungs: crackles both bases, a little higher than in February. No edema.

A/P: Progressive dyspnea in RA-ILD, on methotrexate and amiodarone, both of which can affect the lungs. Called pulmonology - they will see her early August with repeat imaging and PFTs. Quarterly MTX labs today. Return precautions reviewed in detail.

conditions.label: Chronic drug-induced interstitial lung disorders
conditions.note: Amiodarone-induced pulmonary toxicity, superimposed on RA-ILD

social.value: Caregiver for her father; former administrative assistant

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Diffuse interstitial opacities. Heart size normal. No effusion or pneumothorax. Right axillary clips.
High-resolution CT chest without contrast. Reticular pattern with areas of honeycombing. No pleural effusion. No consolidation or mass. Heart size normal.
reports.conclusion: Fibrotic interstitial lung disease with honeycombing, progressed since 9/2022.

reports.text: Spirometry, plethysmographic lung volumes and diffusing capacity. Acceptable effort. Total lung capacity reduced. DLCO reduced.
reports.conclusion: Restrictive pattern with reduced diffusing capacity.

documents.title: Pulmonology follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Seen 8/7/2024 at her PCP's request, earlier than her yearly visit.

History: about four months of steadily worsening breathlessness. She first thought she was out of shape, but now cannot walk a block without stopping. The dry cough never produces anything. No fevers, chills or weight loss. Eating a little less because she is short of breath when she eats. No chest pain, orthopnea or ankle swelling. Her RA joint pain has been mostly controlled, with some morning stiffness. She has taken methotrexate for several years with prednisone 5 mg and occasional NSAIDs, and amiodarone 200 mg daily since 2016.

Social: her father fell ill last year and she moved in to care for him - cooking, cleaning, managing his pills. He has recently moved across the state for better insurance coverage; she misses him and is also glad of the time back. She grows rare plants in a greenhouse, collected on years of trips abroad, and is now winded watering and repotting. Never smoker, no alcohol or drugs. No asbestos, silica or coal dust exposure.

Exam: SpO2 91% on room air, RR 21, BP 122/74, afebrile. Mildly dyspneic at rest. Heart regular without murmur. End-inspiratory crackles both lungs, loudest at the bases; no wheeze or rhonchi. Clubbing of the fingers. Mild hand deformities from longstanding RA, no active synovitis.

Studies: chest film with diffuse interstitial opacities. HRCT with a reticular pattern and areas of honeycombing, clearly worse than 2022. PFTs restrictive with reduced TLC and reduced DLCO.

Impression: amiodarone-induced pulmonary toxicity on a background of RA-associated interstitial lung disease, with significant progression.

Plan: stop amiodarone now. I have spoken with her cardiologist, who agrees and will see her to plan rhythm management. Rheumatology will review her DMARD regimen in light of the progression. Follow-up here in about 4 months.

documents.title: Amiodarone stopped
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed pulm letter. Called pt: she stopped amiodarone on 8/8 as instructed. Cardiology visit set for September. Rheum appointment in October to discuss changing RA meds. No palpitations. Med list updated - amiodarone removed. Explained it can take months for lungs to improve after stopping, if they do. She asked whether she should give up the greenhouse; told her pulm can weigh in but no evidence it is the cause.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 72. PR 178 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 440 ms. No ST-T change.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Seen 9/18/2024, six weeks after amiodarone was stopped for pulmonary toxicity. No palpitations since stopping. ECG sinus rhythm.

We will not start another antiarrhythmic for now, given how infrequent her atrial fibrillation has been; if it recurs we will discuss options. CHA2DS2-VASc remains 1 (female sex), so anticoagulation is still not indicated. She knows to report palpitations. Return in 6 months.

documents.title: Ophthalmology report
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body: Hydroxychloroquine screening 9/25/2024. Visual fields and SD-OCT normal. No toxicity. Continue yearly while on the drug.

documents.title: Vaccines

documents.body: Flu and COVID vaccines given, separate arms. Given ahead of her new RA infusion next week so they have time to work. Labs drawn for rheum.

medications.reason: Switched to rituximab; progressive lung disease

medications.sig: 1000 mg IV infusion every 6 months at the rheumatology infusion center
medications.reason: Rheumatoid arthritis with interstitial lung disease

documents.title: Rheumatology visit and infusion
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Seen 10/21/2024.

Given the progression of her interstitial lung disease and only partial control of her arthritis on methotrexate, after earlier failure of infliximab and diclofenac and with ongoing prednisone, we have changed her treatment to rituximab. Hepatitis B surface antigen negative this morning. First infusion of rituximab 1000 mg IV given today with premedication, tolerated without reaction. She will receive 1000 mg every 6 months.

Stopped: methotrexate, folic acid and hydroxychloroquine. Continue prednisone 5 mg daily and esomeprazole. She knows to call with fever or infection symptoms; her vaccines were updated last week.

Next infusion in about 6 months. A CBC before each course would be appreciated.

documents.title: Insurance letter
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Insurer faxed a notice that rituximab was approved under medical benefit for 12 months (request by rheumatology). Scanned for reference. Also faxed renewal for esomeprazole quantity limit - completed and returned, PCP signed.

reports.text: Bilateral diagnostic mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison 2022 and 2023. Scattered fibroglandular density. Stable right post-lumpectomy change. No suspicious finding.

documents.title: Mammogram result
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Benign. Mailed letter.

documents.title: Pulmonology follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Seen 12/4/2024, four months after amiodarone was stopped. She feels her breathing is a little better; she can get through watering the greenhouse with one rest. Cough unchanged. Now on rituximab per rheumatology.

SpO2 93% on room air at rest. Crackles at both bases, unchanged.

Impression: amiodarone pulmonary toxicity with RA-ILD, modest improvement off amiodarone.

Plan: continue current treatment. She was counseled to seek care early for fever or productive cough given her immunosuppression. Follow-up in about 9 months, sooner if worse.
